seo.title: Bathroom Brands We Fit in Crowthorne | Fit-Only Installation | Install My Bathroom
seo.description: The sanitaryware, brassware and tile brands we fit for Crowthorne clients, and how our fit-only installation model works alongside your own supplier choices.

h1: Bathroom Brands We Fit in Crowthorne

hero.intro: We don't sell bathrooms in Crowthorne — we fit them. That's the fit-only model in a sentence: you choose and buy your own sanitaryware, brassware, tiles and furniture, from whichever showroom or retailer you prefer, and we install it to the standard the brand and your room both deserve. Over 30 years of fitting high-end bathrooms, certain brands turn up on our Crowthorne specification sheets more often than others — some suited to the period detail of the substantial Victorian and Edwardian houses near Wellington College, others just as at home in the village's newer family housing — each with its own installation detail that matters more than most people expect before the first fixing goes into the wall.

sections.heading: The fit-only model explained
sections.body: Nothing about the fit-only model changes which brands you can bring to a Crowthorne installation — if anything, it widens the choice, because we're not trying to steer you toward stock we hold or a supplier we have an arrangement with. You buy from the showroom or retailer you trust, at the price you've agreed, and we check it all at survey: waste sizes, tap centres, fixing requirements and whether everything you've chosen is actually compatible with everything else, before strip-out starts rather than after a delivery is already sitting in the hallway.

sections.heading: Sanitaryware and shower toilets we fit
sections.body: Geberit's concealed cisterns, wall-hung WCs and AquaClean shower toilets are the sanitaryware brand we fit most often in Crowthorne, and correct frame selection matters more here than with most brands, because the cistern and pan weight sits entirely on the carrier frame rather than the wall tiles — a detail worth getting right in an older masonry-walled house as much as a modern one. We also fit a good deal of Villeroy & Boch, bought through showrooms and retailers across Berkshire — precise ceramics and hard-wearing glaze finishes, with flush plate, pan and frame generations checked for compatibility before anything is ordered. Where Duravit is specified, it's usually alongside SensoWash shower toilet seats or a full ME by Starck suite, and the detail worth settling early is whether the installation route is Duravit's own DuraSystem frame or a standard concealed cistern frame — the two aren't interchangeable once a wall is boarded. On a handful of more specified Crowthorne projects, TOTO's Washlet or Neorest ranges turn up, and we plan the first fix differently depending on which one it is, since a Washlet seat adds to a conventional pan while a Neorest replaces the pan, cistern and seat as a single integrated unit.

sections.heading: Brassware and showers we fit
sections.body: hansgrohe brassware and shower systems appear on more of our Crowthorne specification sheets than almost any other single brand, usually paired with sanitaryware from Duravit, Villeroy & Boch or Laufen — the engineering is consistent, so performance comes down to water pressure, rough-in depth and whether the valve body was set correctly before the wall closed up. Grohe covers a wide span of the work we do here too, from thermostatic shower valves and mixer taps on mid-range refits through to Rapid SL cistern frames and digital shower products on more specified projects, which is why we work through exactly what's been chosen at survey rather than treating every Grohe job the same way. On the more design-led end, AXOR — hansgrohe's design brand built around collaborations such as AXOR Starck and AXOR Citterio — turns up in some of Crowthorne's more considered refits, and the finish is the detail that separates a good installation from an average one: a brushed or matte black trim shows every scuff mark from a careless fit in a way chrome never does, so handling and sequencing get more attention than usual.

sections.heading: Baths, trays and period-style brassware we fit
sections.body: Victoria + Albert's freestanding baths are cast from a volcanic limestone and resin composite rather than acrylic or steel, giving genuine weight and a cool, solid surface — a point that matters as much to how the bath gets into the room as to how it sits once installed, and on an older suspended timber floor, to how that weight is supported underneath it. Kaldewei's titanium-enamelled steel baths and shower trays are rigid rather than flexible, so the installation detail is about even, accurate bearing across the full base rather than preventing flex the way an acrylic bath support does. Where a Crowthorne client wants brassware that suits a Victorian or Edwardian house rather than a contemporary one, Lefroy Brooks and Burlington both turn up — traditional cross-head handles, exposed pipework and period-inspired profiles built around a modern fixing standard underneath, where every joint, bracket and pipe run is set out to be looked at rather than hidden. Matki's largely frameless shower enclosures leave very little trim to hide an inaccurate opening, so measuring, wall fixing and sequencing against tiling and the tray get planned in that order, not worked out on the day.

sections.heading: Choosing brands for Crowthorne's period and newer homes
sections.body: Crowthorne's character comes partly from its association with Wellington College, and the substantial Victorian and Edwardian houses that line the surrounding roads tend to have solid masonry walls and, on the ground floor, a higher chance of suspended timber construction than the twentieth-century family housing and newer infill further from the centre. That mix doesn't dictate which brands suit which property — a Geberit frame or a Matki frameless screen fits into a Victorian house as readily as a newer family home once the wall or floor underneath has been properly checked — but it does change what gets checked first. A heavy Victoria + Albert composite bath or a rigid Kaldewei steel tray needs that suspended timber floor confirmed for deflection before it goes anywhere near the room, which is exactly what the survey is for, whichever brand ends up being specified.

faqs.q: Do I have to buy my bathroom from you?
faqs.a: No. We're fit-only — you buy your sanitaryware, brassware, tiles and furniture from whichever showroom or retailer you choose, and we install it.

faqs.q: Can you fit a bathroom with products from several different brands mixed together?
faqs.a: Yes, this is the norm. We check waste sizes, tap centres and fixing requirements across every brand involved at survey, so everything is confirmed compatible before strip-out starts.

faqs.q: Do you have a preferred brand you push clients toward?
faqs.a: No. The fit-only model means we don't hold stock or have a sales arrangement with any particular manufacturer — the brands mentioned here are simply the ones that appear most often on the specifications our Crowthorne clients bring to us.

faqs.q: Can traditional brassware like Lefroy Brooks or Burlington suit a Victorian Crowthorne house?
faqs.a: Yes, and it's a common choice for the village's period properties. These ranges are built around exposed pipework and period-inspired profiles, which we fit so the pipe runs, brackets and fixings are set out and finished to be looked at, not hidden.

faqs.q: Does a heavy freestanding bath need anything extra checking in an older Crowthorne house?
faqs.a: Often, yes. A Victoria + Albert composite bath or a Kaldewei steel bath has real weight and needs accurate, even bearing underneath it — on a ground floor with suspended timber construction, we confirm that structural support at survey before the bath is ordered.

faqs.q: Will you fit products bought from an online retailer rather than a showroom?
faqs.a: Yes, provided the specification is confirmed compatible at survey. We check this regardless of where a product was bought from.

image.heroPrompt: Purpose: hero image for the Crowthorne brands page, a close/mid detail shot implying a choice between traditional and contemporary brand character rather than a full room. Subject and action: a traditional cross-head exposed shower valve with visible pipework mounted beside a stone-topped vanity carrying a sleek contemporary basin mixer, the two styles placed close together as if mid-way through a specification decision, no running water. Setting and work-stage: a finished bathroom wall inside a renovated Crowthorne house blending period and modern fittings, midday, bright daylight entering from an unseen window to the side. Composition: close-to-fixture mid shot centred where the exposed traditional pipework meets the contemporary vanity edge, dark stone surface filling the lower third of the frame, wall tiling soft and slightly out of focus behind. Light and materials: dark basalt stone vanity top with natural flecking, brushed chrome exposed pipework and cross-head valve alongside a brushed chrome contemporary mixer tap, bright midday daylight raking across the stone at a shallow angle, creating uneven highlight and shadow rather than flat light. Constraints: no people, no text, no logos, no brand names visible on any fixture; no LED lighting strips anywhere in frame; no symmetrical twin-basin staging; no uniform gold or amber colour wash; no hanging plants, florals or candles; no water shown running; fixtures should show faint, believable handling marks rather than uniform showroom-new gloss.
image.heroAlt: Close-up of a traditional exposed brushed chrome shower valve beside a contemporary basin mixer on a dark basalt stone vanity top in a Crowthorne bathroom
